purpose: Keep the AEP understanding, generation, migration, and cleanup work on a machine-readable mainline so large execution does not drift into ad hoc validation or documentation churn.

user_goals: Cross-platform where possible; AE-host-only validation is allowed when the host is inherently required.
Prefer Go tools over PowerShell for new planning, registry, audit, and summarization work.
Eventually support automatic AEP learning, reusable skill extraction, workflow generation, and possible AI-driven project generation.
Parse detailed AEP information instead of only proving round-trip smoke behavior.
Convert versions as losslessly as possible, with explicit boundaries for high-version-only features.
Support AE2020+ now and leave an explicit expansion path for AE2026, AE2027, and later versions.
Keep commercial value in view: reusable conversion, validation, learning, generation, and project inspection workflows.
background.current_problem: Data, examples, fixtures, generated evidence, and project state are spread across data, examples, test_data, tmp, internal serializer templates, and flightdeck work files. Large validation work must become total-summary / detailed-work / total-summary instead of scattered manual notes.

principles.rule: Before executing a large phase, update or create a machine-readable spec that defines scope, artifacts, gates, and next actions.
Prefer JSON source-of-truth artifacts over long mutable markdown plans. Markdown may summarize JSON, but must not be the authoritative ledger.
Use Go for new registry, audit, inventory, ownership, summarization, and orchestration where practical. PowerShell may remain for AE host orchestration until replaced safely.
Do not delete, move, or rename data until the relevant location, ownership, and evidence reports identify what the asset is and why it is safe to change.
Large validation work must have a total plan/ledger, detailed per-atom execution, and a regenerated total summary.
Batch related verification or registry updates into scoped commits. Avoid many tiny commits for repeated validation-only work.

phases.objective: Create a machine-readable registry and Go audit surface before data cleanup.
Make asset distribution and ownership visible enough to guide cleanup and atomization.
allowed_work: Improve aepregistry inventory and ownership reports.
Add generated JSON reports under tmp.
Add tests for report semantics and deterministic summaries.
not_allowed_work: Mark large unowned regions as owned without atom/evidence justification.
Create new long-lived markdown plans for the same state.
exit_criteria: registry audit passes with zero errors.
inventory report identifies all registered locations and missing locations.
ownership report identifies owned and unowned files by location and gives grouped priorities for major unowned regions.
The next atomization target can be selected from JSON evidence, not memory.

phases.objective: Expand capability atoms from representative samples toward coverage of recipes, templates, fixtures, and version evidence.
entry_criteria: A specific location or domain is selected from ownership groups.
expected_outputs: Reduced unowned count for selected domain or an explicit boundary reason

phases.objective: Bring AE2020-AE2025 migration validation into a total/detail/total JSON ledger by atom and version axis.
entry_criteria: Atom taxonomy exists for the selected validation domain.
Existing historical matrix outputs are registered or intentionally excluded.

version_axis.expansion_policy: Add AE2026/AE2027 as data entries after writers, fixtures, host paths, and evidence gates are registered.

expected_outputs: Machine-readable matrix summary by atom and version.
Direct vs inferred host-open labels are explicit.
Known source-contract boundaries are not counted as unexplained failures.

last_completed_target.reason: Register directory-level template-library atoms for serializer template source contracts so tracked template files are owned before any cleanup or migration planning.

previous_target.reason: Add a generated JSON report that combines location inventory and ownership into cleanup actions, so generated/untracked cleanup candidates are separated from tracked/required files that must be atomized or registered first.

boundary_notes: minimal-layer-explicit-matte remains covered by layer.track_matte.explicit_source as a version-boundary atom, not a pass-complete layer atom.

current_execution.next_action: Use tmp/registry_layout.json to pick the next cleanup-safe atomization target. serializer_templates is now fully owned; the next highest-impact tracked blocker is fixture_generators with 239 unowned files. Generated cleanup candidates must stay review-only until their producing workflows are identified.
must_not_skip: Run registry audit after report changes.
Run registry ownership after atom taxonomy changes.
Run focused Go tests for internal/registry and cmd/aepregistry.
Run full go test ./... before claiming completion of a committed Go change.
